channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Why Apple Vision Pro Is Struggling Compared to Meta’s VR Glasses
item.description: On this episode of the Power On podcast, Mark Gurman addresses backlash over his Vision Pro coverage, reporting that even top Apple executives don't use the heavy, expensive headset. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Who Pays for AI: Financing the Next Investment Cycle
item.description: AI is driving one of the largest capital spending cycles in decades, creating new questions around how that investment will be financed and where the risks and opportunities will emerge across credit markets. PIMCO’s Lotfi Karoui, Goldman Sachs’ Amanda Lynam and Barclays’ Brad Rogoff joined Bloomberg’s Romaine Bostick at the Bloomberg Future of Fixed Income 2026 conference in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Citrini Says Agentic Finance Fosters ‘New Paradigm’ for Crypto Investing
item.description: Citrini Research is making the case that a “new paradigm of ‘fundamental crypto investing’” has arrived because agentic finance will be built on top of blockchains.
item.dc:creator: Muyao Shen

item.title: Union Square Ventures Doubles Fund Size for the AI Era
item.description: New York City-based venture firm Union Square Ventures is reinventing itself to better compete in the AI race by nearly doubling the size of its core fund, raising $900 million in new money, including $500 million for its latest early-stage fund. The firm is also whittling down its general partnership to just four investors - including Nick Grossman. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple Names Steve Smith M&A Chief, Moves Adrian Perica to Services Business
item.description: Apple Inc. is naming a new mergers and acquisitions chief, according to people familiar with the matter, marking the latest management change under new Chief Executive Officer John Ternus.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: AI Spending Questions Persist as Washington Targets Tech Visas
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down the Trump administration's decision to suspend an immigration program for multiple tech firms, including Microsoft, alleging widespread abuse of that worker visa system. Plus: Samsung's quarterly profit jumps and TSMC sales surge, but investors are still worried about the staying power of the AI investment boom. And, NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 makes it way back down to Earth after 237 days in space. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia-Backed Firmus Is Set to Postpone IPO, Weigh Private Round
item.description: Australian data center company Firmus Grid Ltd. is set to postpone its initial public offering, and the company is weighing a private funding round instead, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Julia Fioretti, Manuel Baigorri and Anthony Hughes

item.title: OpenAI’s Revenue Run Rate Nears $50 Billion, Less Than Reported
item.description: OpenAI is on track to generate annualized revenue of roughly $50 billion based on its current performance, according to people familiar with the matter, an uptick from the prior year but less than some recently reported estimates for the ChatGPT maker.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence and Shirin Ghaffary

item.title: FTC Probes Block After Consumer Complaints Over Frozen Accounts
item.description: The Federal Trade Commission is investigating whether Block Inc., the parent of Square and Cash App, violated US consumer protection laws by failing to provide adequate customer service to help with frozen or deactivated accounts amid significant cuts in staffing.
item.dc:creator: Leah Nylen

item.title: Oracle Moves Gas by Trucks to Avoid Data Center Power Delays
item.description: Oracle Corp. is using a novel power strategy to keep several data centers on track: trucking natural gas directly to the server farms.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford and Julian Hast

item.title: Senate Democrats Demand Apology From GOP Over Jack Smith Hearing
item.description: Senate Judiciary Committee Democrats have requested that panel chair, Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa), apologize to ex-special counsel Jack Smith on behalf of his Republican colleagues following a contentious hearing in September.
item.dc:creator: Claire Bernard

item.title: Inside John Ternus’ New Apple + Meta’s Vision Pro Killer
item.description:
In this episode of Power On, Mark Gurman and Bloomberg tech editor Vlad Savov unpack John Ternus’ first month running Apple — from his push to make the company leaner and faster to his unusually hands-on role overseeing design. They discuss why more layoffs could be coming, how Ternus is putting design back at the center of Apple and why Tim Cook, now executive chairman, remains the company’s face on the world stage. Then, Mark gives his verdict on Meta’s new $1,299 VR glasses after trying them himself — and explains why they are the device Apple’s Vision Pro should have been all along.
Have a question for Mark? Email us at poweron@bloomberg.net or join the Power On Discord
Subscribe to the Power On Newsletter at https://www.bloomberg.com/poweron (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple Announces Oct. 13 Smart Home Product Launch in New York
item.description: Apple Inc. on Thursday confirmed it will hold an Oct. 13 product launch in New York to introduce new smart home products.
item.dc:creator: Chris Welch

item.title: Britain’s Great Wealth Dilemma
item.description: Individuals behind a combined $160 billion are leaving London as UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham tries to balance tax fairness with revenue. The exodus has raised questions about the city’s status as a wealth hub. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Model Evaluator Arena Valued at Over $3 Billion in Round
item.description: Arena Intelligence Inc., the startup behind a popular artificial intelligence model leaderboard, has raised $200 million in funding at a $3.1 billion valuation and plans to expand into measuring AI safety, tapping into growing demand to evaluate the technology’s performance and risks.The financing, set to be announced Thursday, was led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Khosla Ventures, with participation from Salesforce Ventures and Dell Technologies Capital. item.dc:creator: Rachel Metz

item.title: CreditSights' Cisar Sees Cracks in AI Credit Boom
item.description: Winnie Cisar, global head of strategy at CreditSights, says the surge in AI financing is making credit analysis increasingly difficult as investors weigh uncertain returns, potential data center overbuilding and more complex financing structures. She speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: GlobalFoundries Rallies After Announcing $2 Billion TSMC Deal
item.description: GlobalFoundries Inc. shares gained as much as 7% after the chip manufacturer announced a five-year, $2 billion deal to provide US production capacity to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.
item.dc:creator: Ian King

item.title: Nigeria-Founded Moove to Exit Country After Uber Pulled Out
item.description: Moove, the Nigerian-founded mobility startup valued at $2.1 billion, plans to exit the African country after Uber Technologies Inc. closed its operations in early September.
item.dc:creator: Loni Prinsloo

item.title: What Everyone Gets Wrong About the Economic Problems in Europe
item.description: It has been two years since the publication of the Draghi report and the problems the report identified about European competitiveness are far from solved: Demographic challenges, rising energy costs, and a lagging tech sector still cast a shadow over Europe. But according to the economist and policy analyst Dominik Leusder (who also writes the Leusder of Last Resort Substack) the Draghi report might have mismeasured the true scale of Europe's issues, and he asks if the popular narrative of European decline is an accurate one. We also speak about whether Europe needs a frontier AI model, why long, wine-soaked lunches are not a good way to measure productivity, and the state of Europe's vexed relationship with China as a trade partner and competitor. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Musk Asks If Ambani Is ‘Real Boss of India’ in Fresh Jibe
item.description: Elon Musk stepped up his criticism of Indian rivals with a direct swipe at billionaire Mukesh Ambani, as SpaceX’s Starlink satellite broadband network continues to await regulatory approval for a rollout in the country.
item.dc:creator: Alisha Sachdev
